LESSON: ISLAM IN KENYA • COAST • WESTERN • CENTRAL • NORTH EASTERN KENYA

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Islamic Heritage and Civilisation
Topic 7.1: Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 7

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya, part of Islamic Heritage and Civilisation in Grade 9 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: What factors facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya? 2. What was the impact of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the factors that facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives as a factor of civilisation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. examine the challenges faced by the early Muslims in the propagation of Islam,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the contribution of Islam to the development of culture in Kenya.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the factors that facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya,

   Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. explain the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives as a factor of civilisation,

   Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. examine the challenges faced by the early Muslims in the propagation of Islam,

   Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the contribution of Islam to the development of culture in Kenya.

   Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. describe the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Kenya (Coast, Western, Central, and North Eastern) in groups and present on charts/PowerPoint,

2. research on the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives and make notes,

3. watch video clips on the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives,

4. model old architectural designs of mosques, doors, mats, wudhu vessels, and sandals,

5. modelling activities adorning the Islamic cultural mode of dressing introduced by the Arabs, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. describe the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Kenya (Coast, Western, Central, and North Eastern) in groups and present on charts/PowerPoint,
2. research on the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives and make notes,
3. watch video clips on the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives,
4. model old architectural designs of mosques, doors, mats, wudhu vessels, and sandals,
5. modelling activities adorning the Islamic cultural mode of dressing introduced by the Arabs, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Islam in Kenya • Coast • Western • Central • North Eastern Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: the skill of carrying out research is enhanced as learners seek information on the effects of the

contact between the early Muslims and the natives.

• Communication and Collaboration: the skill of listening, speaking, and teamwork is enhanced as learners discuss

the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Kenya.

• Self-efficacy: the skill of effective communication enhanced as learners research online/read from available reference

materials on the challenges faced by the early Muslims as they propagated Islam and shares in class.

• Creativity and Imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners model old architectural designs of mosques,

doors, mats, wudhu vessels, and sandals.

Values:
• Unity is enhanced as learners discuss the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Kenya (Coast, Western, Central, and

North Eastern) in groups.

• Responsibility enhanced as learners research on the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Ethnic and racial relations enhanced as learners research on the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the

natives.

Link to other Subjects:

Social Studies as learners discuss the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Kenya (Coast, Western, Central, and North

Eastern) in groups.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the factors that facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya,
2. explain the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives as a factor of civilisation,
3. examine the challenges faced by the early Muslims in the propagation of Islam,
4. appreciate the contribution of Islam to the development of culture in Kenya.

Remember the key question: What factors facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya? 2. What was the impact of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives?
